extracted.intended_audience: GSA staff, contracting officers, regulated industry, and other rulemaking stakeholders (including small businesses and commenters)
extracted.subtask_short: writing Federal Register Unified Agenda entries
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required fields for preparing and publishing Unified Agenda/Federal Register entries (here, GSA proposed rule entries), including required metadata, abstracts, timetable items, and Regulatory Flexibility Act printing limits. Useful for agency drafters, rule writers, and stakeholders who must read or verify Federal Register/Unified Agenda content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status of FederalRegister.gov XML edition
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a “Web 2.0” version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register, and does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on GPO’s govinfo.gov. ... This prototype edition of the daily Federal Register on FederalRegister.gov will remain an unofficial informational resource until the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register (ACFR) issues a regulation granting it official legal status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents posted are XML renditions; each includes a link to the corresponding official PDF on govinfo.gov. Those relying on it for legal research should verify results against an official edition of the Federal Register. Until ACFR grants official status, the XML rendition does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing limitations for Unified Agenda entries under the Regulatory Flexibility Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Because publication in the Federal Register is mandated for the regulatory flexibility agendas required by the Regulatory Flexibility Act (5 U.S.C. 602), GSA's printed agenda entries include only: (1) Rules that are in the Agency's regulatory flexibility agenda, in accordance with the Regulatory Flexibility Act, because they are likely to have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; and (2) Any rules that the Agency has identified for periodic review under section 610 of the Regulatory Flexibility Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printing of these entries is limited to fields that contain information required by the Regulatory Flexibility Act's Agenda requirements. Additional information on these entries is available in the Unified Agenda published on the internet (www.reginfo.gov). Use the online Unified Agenda for fuller entries; the Federal Register print entry is intentionally limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Headings required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Document headings vary by document type but may contain the following: the agency or agencies that issued and signed a document; the number of the CFR title and the number of each part the document amends, proposes to amend, or is directly related to; the agency docket number / agency internal file number; the RIN which identifies each regulatory action listed in the Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Document Drafting Handbook for more detail. The headings form internal navigation links (table of contents) but that repetition has no substantive legal effect; include the listed items to conform to standard Federal Register drafting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official PDF for legal/electronic official format
rubrics_metrics.description: This document has been published in the Federal Register. Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar for the official electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing or relying on the official text, use the PDF on govinfo.gov (or other official editions). The FederalRegister.gov XML is informative but not the official source for legal citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Inspection verification requirement and legal notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are using public inspection listings for legal research, you should verify the contents of the documents against a final, official edition of the Federal Register. Only official editions of the Federal Register provide legal notice of publication to the public and judicial notice to the courts under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume public inspection listings or the prototype XML establish legal notice; always verify against the final official edition to ensure legal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable fields for Unified Agenda / rulemaking entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Timetable entries identify actions and dates (examples shown include: Action, Date, FR Cite; ANPRM, ANPRM Comment Period End; NPRM, NPRM Comment Period End).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include each significant procedural milestone (e.g., ANPRM, ANPRM comment end, NPRM, NPRM comment end, final rule actions) with corresponding dates and Federal Register citations where applicable. Indicate whether a Regulatory Flexibility Analysis is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Details / metadata fields to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Document Details shown include Agency; CFR; Document Citation (e.g., 86 FR 41286); Document Number; Document Type (e.g., Proposed Rule); Pages; Publication Date; PDF Official Content. Additional enhanced content includes Table of Contents, Public Comments, Regulations.gov Data, Sharing, Document Statistics, Other Formats (JSON, XML, MODS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete metadata so readers can locate the official text (FR citation, document number, pages, PDF link) and access auxiliary formats (XML, JSON) and developer tools. Present the Agency and CFR references clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract and Legal Authority in proposed-rule entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed rule entry includes a 'Legal Authority' citation and an 'Abstract' summarizing the proposed amendments (for example: 'Legal Authority: 40 U.S.C. 121(c)' followed by an abstract describing the purpose, scope, and effect of the proposed GSAR amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts should concisely describe the rule's objective, scope (e.g., which GSAR parts or clauses are amended), and practical effect (e.g., incorporating cybersecurity requirements into GSAR). Always state the legal authority supporting the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency contact information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry provides 'Agency Contact' information listing a named official, title/office, mailing address, phone number, and email (e.g., 'Agency Contact: Johnnie McDowell, Procurement Analyst, GSA Acquisition Policy Division ... Phone: 202 718-6112, Email: johnnie.mcdowell@gsa.gov').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete contact details so interested persons can ask for further information; include name, role/division, postal address, phone, and email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Analysis Required flag
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries indicate whether a Regulatory Flexibility Analysis is required (examples shown: 'Regulatory Flexibility Analysis Required: Yes.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state whether the Regulatory Flexibility Act analysis is required; this affects the content and extent of information printed in the Federal Register and the Unified Agenda entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing external rulemaking resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Published proposed rules may be reviewed in their entirety at the Government's rulemaking website at http://www.regulations.gov. Since the fall 2007 edition, the internet has been the basic means for disseminating the Unified Agenda. The complete Unified Agenda will be available online at www.reginfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links to regulations.gov and reginfo.gov for full rule texts, supporting documents, and additional agenda details. Use online resources to present fuller context than the printed Federal Register entry.
